title: Distributed Cache & Resilient Read-Through Review
description: Inspect a distributed caching function for unpooled client connection exhaustion, cache stampede thundering herd vulnerabilities, and blocking KEYS command usage.

artifact.content:
import time
import redis

def fetch_user_profile(user_id: str, db_pool):
    # Creates unpooled raw Redis client on every single request causing connection exhaustion
    client = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, db=0)
    cache_key = f'user:profile:{user_id}'
    cached = client.get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return cached

    # Cache stampede: concurrent requests all query database directly without distributed lock
    data = db_pool.query_user(user_id)
    # Unbounded key scanning blocking Redis event loop instead of targeted pipeline
    all_keys = client.keys('user:profile:*')
    client.set(cache_key, str(data), ex=300)
    return data

defects.title: Unpooled Redis Client Instantiation per Request
defects.consequence: Creating a new Redis connection object on every function call exhausts OS socket descriptors and introduces severe TCP handshake latency overhead under load.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Instantiate a persistent Redis ConnectionPool once at application startup and share it across calls.

defects.title: Cache Stampede Thundering Herd Vulnerability
defects.consequence: When a popular cache key expires, multiple concurrent requests simultaneously query the primary database, overwhelming database connection pools.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Implement distributed locking (e.g. Redlock or singleflight pattern) to ensure only one process rebuilds the cache.

defects.title: Blocking KEYS Command Execution in Production
defects.consequence: The KEYS command iterates over all keys in the single-threaded Redis database synchronously, freezing all Redis operations for the entire application cluster.
defects.diagnostic_explanation: Avoid KEYS in production. Use SCAN with cursor pagination or maintain a dedicated set of keys.
